title: Extension Figures Carried by Each Keyturn Trip Booking Rate Plan
content:
A guest keeping a Keyturn Trip Booking vehicle for longer meets five figures that belong to the reservation's rate plan: the hours before the scheduled return by which an extension must be asked for, the longest extension the plan allows on one reservation, the uplift applied to the daily rate for extended time, the hours the host has to decide the request, and the miles included for each 24 hours of extended time.

| Rate plan | Lead time before the scheduled return (hours) | Longest extension on one reservation (hours) | Uplift on the daily rate (per cent) | Host decision window (hours) | Included miles for each 24 hours of extended time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keyturn Hourly Rate Plan | 0.5 | 6 | 0 | 0.5 | 60 |
| Keyturn Daily Rate Plan | 4 | 24 | 5 | 2 | 200 |
| Keyturn Weekend Rate Plan | 6 | 24 | 5 | 3 | 250 |
| Keyturn Weekly Rate Plan | 12 | 72 | 8 | 6 | 175 |
| Keyturn Monthly Rate Plan | 24 | 168 | 10 | 12 | 125 |
| Keyturn Extended Stay Rate Plan | 48 | 720 | 12 | 24 | 100 |

### Notes on the figures

The lead time and the decision window are both stated in hours and both widen with the plan, the lead time from half an hour to 48 hours and the decision window from half an hour to 24 hours. The longest extension the plan allows widens far more steeply, from 6 hours on the Keyturn Hourly Rate Plan to 720 hours on the Keyturn Extended Stay Rate Plan.

The uplift stands at 0 per cent on the Keyturn Hourly Rate Plan, which is to say that plan publishes no uplift on extended time, and rises to 12 per cent at the top of the ladder. The included miles for each 24 hours of extended time match, plan for plan, the miles the plan includes for each 24 hours of reserved time.
